[IALC.3.6] **An allocation failure in the regex engine is an allocation
failure like any other.** The C++ seam must catch a failed allocation in every
function it exports to C, so that no C++ exception crosses into libds's C code,
and must report the failure to its caller ([IERR.8.7]). The caller must
surface it as it surfaces a failed allocation at the same site: compiling a
pattern while an artefact loads refuses the load with `DS_ERR_OOM`; a match or
a capture after the load, in an alpha `REGEX` test as a fact propagates or in a
builtin during a firing, is the EngineError ALLOCATION, which halts the tier
([LERR.1.4.7]). These are the three places [IALC.3.5] lists, and at none of
them is a failed allocation read as a non-match.
